punchline: Turning a thermostat to the top does not warm the room faster, because the dial only decides when the heating stops.
thirty_sec: Don Norman describes a thermostat that people crank to the top to heat a cold room faster. It makes no difference: the dial only decides when the heating shuts off. His fridge has two controls, freezer and fresh food, that look independent but are not. Make the freezer colder and the salad freezes. Norman says the controls suggest a false conceptual model in the user's head.
